answer: At an inlet to an agent marketplace, make each fresh identity solve a randomized, memory-bound puzzle before it can bid, and cap attempts per network over time. A Sybil farm must buy compute and bandwidth for every identity, while rising costs slow bursts; independent peers can flag clusters. It still cannot stop a well-funded attacker renting machines, and network limits can disadvantage shared households, so provide appeals and never treat puzzle success as proof of personhood. An orchard of useful agents should stay open to newcomers; a summit review can challenge suspicious patterns.
